newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West spot power prices mostly unchanged.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West spot power prices mostly unchanged.

text.p: Spot power prices in the western U.S. were steady Monday amid somewhat cooler-than-normal temperatures in the Northwest and continued strength in natural gas prices, trade sources.
"The weather is a little bit cooler, but nobody really seems to have that big of a need to buy," said one Northwest trader.
According to the latest 6- to 10-day forecast, high temperatures in the Pacific Northwest are seen running 3-5 degrees Fahrenheit below normal, but low temperatures are seen 3-5 degrees above normal.
Temperatures in the Southwest are expected to be warmer than normal due to easterly Santa Ana winds off the desert.
Next-day prices at the California-Oregon border (COB) were last quoted $19.25-19.75 per megawatt hour (MWh), unchanged from Friday.
Cash November quotes for COB were seen at $18.75-18.95.
Mid-Columbia prices were also little changed at $17.25-18.00 for peak power and $15.25-16.00 for off-peak.
In the Southwest, next-day Palo Verde power was quoted $17.75-18.75 per MWh, unchanged from Friday.
Traders also cited firmer spot natural gas prices as contributing to the steady tone in the power market.
